outcome: Immediate complications (pelvic pain, urticaria, puncture site hematoma)
cohort: A retrospective cohort of 227 patients aged 19-47 years who underwent uterine artery embolization for intractable postpartum hemorrhage between September 2011 and September 2021, categorized by the presence or absence of Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
finding: Uterine artery embolization is a safe and effective method to control intractable postpartum hemorrhage, showing no significant difference in technical or clinical success rates between patients with and without placenta accreta spectrum.
